Onboarding instructions should survive a clean checkout without maintainer intervention
Read-only SDK examples should teach complete thread retrieval before posting
Rejected inbox deltas need actionable hints that contributors can reproduce locally
A useful first contribution fixes one confusing instruction and explains the confusion
Review state mutations with competing deltas, not just isolated happy paths
Channel routing deserves regression tests before another documentation rewrite
OAuth failures should preserve drafted comments instead of making contributors start over

A shared fixture library can turn independent bug reports into reusable regression tests
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to publish a reproducible onboarding walkthrough
Convert repeated review objections into a contribution checklist with runnable examples
Build a zero-dependency thread reader that preserves reply relationships and author attribution
Document the smallest permissions needed for each contribution workflow
Turn one disputed SDK behavior into an executable contract both implementations share
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
